segmentMix.title: Segment revenue mix
segmentMix.content:
Axon reports two segments: Connected Devices (TASER conducted energy weapons, body and in-car cameras, drones/counter-drone) and Software & Services (the Axon Evidence cloud platform, Draft One AI report-writing, Axon Records, Carbyne 911, and other recurring subscriptions).

For Axon Enterprise, Inc.: the whole bull case rests on this mix shift -- Software & Services grew roughly 38-43% YoY in 2026 versus Connected Devices' 16-28%, and management bundles hardware with multi-year cloud contracts (the Officer Safety Plan / AI Era Plan) specifically to pull the mix this direction. Higher-margin, recurring Software & Services revenue is why ARR ($1.75B, +40% YoY) and 126% net revenue retention matter more than headline revenue growth.

What to watch:

  • Software & Services as a rising share of total revenue
  • Whether Connected Devices growth is decelerating organically or just normalising after TASER 10 launch comps
  • Any quarter where the mix shift stalls -- it is the market's main justification for the valuation premium

connectedDevicesMix.title: Connected Devices product lines
connectedDevicesMix.content:
Within Connected Devices, TASER is the legacy conducted-energy-weapon franchise (devices, cartridges, warranties); Personal Sensors is body-worn cameras and accessories; Platform Solutions is fleet/in-car video, fixed cameras, drones and counter-drone equipment (Dedrone, Sky-Hero).

For Axon Enterprise, Inc.: Platform Solutions is the fastest-growing and most volatile of the three -- it roughly doubled YoY through much of 2026 on counter-drone deployments, but the FY2026 guidance cut was driven almost entirely by the timing/removal of one large federal Dedrone deployment (~$130m) from this line, not by TASER or Personal Sensors softening.

What to watch:

  • Platform Solutions' lumpiness around large federal/counter-drone orders
  • TASER's growth rate as the TASER 10 upgrade cycle matures
  • Personal Sensors staying roughly flat as the US body-camera market saturates, leaving international and Platform Solutions to carry hardware growth

geoMix.title: US vs International revenue
geoMix.content:
Splits reported revenue between the United States and International (predominantly EMEA) markets.

For Axon Enterprise, Inc.: Axon is still overwhelmingly US-weighted (~82% of revenue) given its roots in US law enforcement, but International is the longer growth runway -- it has been growing faster than the US base and rose from ~16% to ~18% of revenue over the past year as EMEA agencies adopt both CEDs and the cloud platform.

What to watch:

  • International's share of revenue continuing to rise, not just its absolute dollars
  • Large international deals (e.g., the disclosed $21M international TASER 10 agency order) as evidence the ecosystem sell works outside the US
  • Export-control and tariff exposure on CEDs and drone technology, which is concentrated in the international line

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Axon Enterprise, Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Axon Enterprise, Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Axon Enterprise, Inc.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Axon Enterprise, Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Axon Enterprise, Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Axon Enterprise, Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Axon Enterprise, Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Axon Enterprise, Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Axon Enterprise, Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Axon Enterprise, Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
